newsitem.title: FRANCE: Wallenberg could sell Electrolux - paper.
newsitem.headline: Wallenberg could sell Electrolux - paper.

text.p: Sweden's Wallenberg business empire could sell its majority stake in household electronics group Electrolux AB and is in talks with Daewoo Electronics, the La Tribune newspaper said.

"According to our information, the Swedish Wallenberg family has decided to sell one of its most beautiful jewels, Electrolux, the European leader of household electronics, in which it has the majority of voting stock," La Tribune said.
"The group would even be in talks with (South) Korean Daewoo," the paper said, adding that none of the parties concerned had wanted to comment on the information.

On Monday, the head of appliance maker Electrolux, Leif Johansson was called upon to take the helm at Volvo AB and in turn is replaced by Michael Treschow, president and chief executive of industrial engineer Atlas Copco.
Electrolux shares gained on the news on Monday.
Electrolux -- competing with Whirlpool, Samsung and Daewoo as well as France's Moulinex -- on Friday disappointed the market by posting a lower-than-expected profit for calendar 1996.
Profit after financial items slumped 19 percent from a year earlier to 3.25 billion crowns against expectations of a 3.49 billion crown profit while sales fell five percent to 110 billion crowns.
